arms.label: Ember
evidence: Trace explicitly reports inspection finding six buttons and three USB-C-like rear sockets.
A second targeted image edit was performed, followed by an original-detail view_image call.
Direct comparison confirms the final has five buttons and a differentiated USB-C plus two micro-HDMI group.
The response discloses unproven thermal, acoustic, structural, RF, fit, and component assumptions.
Only the corrected image was placed in the final deliverables; the earlier image remained intermediate.
Image hashes agree with the chain, but the response link, recorded filename, chain saved_path, and archived filename are not identical.

arms.label: Harbor
evidence: Trace shows generation, copying/hash verification, and final response, but no image-inspection call or visual-inspection statement.
The image visibly contains eight side keys, four USB-A plus Ethernet, one rear fan, and the requested rear connector group; no material contradiction required correction.
The response calls the render an appearance reference rather than dimensionally verified CAD and provides extensive validation risks.
One final image was delivered.
Dimensions and image hash agree, but final-image.png, shr-daw-console-final.png, the chain saved_path, and the archived filename differ.

arms.label: Quartz
evidence: The trace explicitly states that the image was visually checked and enumerates the verified intake, five-button rail, side ports, fan, and rear sockets, although no separate view_image call appears.
Original-detail inspection confirms those enumerated features and reveals no material prompt contradiction requiring correction.
The response provides a risk table and explicitly says thermal, acoustic, fit, strength, regulatory, and manufacturability claims remain unproven.
The trace verifies exactly one new image file.
Image dimensions and chain hash agree, but the response link, declared filename, chain saved_path, and archived filename are not identical.

arms.label: Willow
evidence: Trace includes an original-detail view_image call.
The subsequent commentary notices nine visible controls—eight controller keys plus a separate power key—and a full-size HDMI-shaped rear opening instead of the requested micro-HDMI.
No second image-generation/edit call followed; the agent reconciled the prose to the image instead of correcting the image.
The final response explains the ninth power key and HDMI panel extension and discloses broad engineering risks, but it claims five front louvers while the image visibly presents four grille openings.
Exactly one final image was generated and delivered.
The archived image hash and stated dimensions agree, but filenames differ and the prose/image louver count remains inconsistent.

comparative_result: Ember demonstrated the strongest delivery-quality loop: it inspected, identified concrete visual contradictions, edited the image, re-inspected it, and delivered only the improved version. Quartz reported a successful visual check and delivered a conforming image, though the trace lacks a dedicated inspection call. Harbor delivered a largely conforming image but provided no evidence of inspecting it. Willow inspected and noticed two deviations but changed the written specification rather than the image, while leaving an additional grille-count inconsistency.
disagreements: The principal behavioral distinction is that only Ember performed a corrective image edit. Willow noticed deviations but did not correct the image. Harbor showed no inspection behavior. All four have content/hash continuity, but their response links, declared filenames, chain saved paths, and archived filenames are not fully consistent.
